description: Fideo Seco is a comforting Mexican pasta dish where thin noodles are toasted and then simmered in a rich, flavorful tomato sauce until tender. This dry version of fideo is a humble yet incredibly satisfying meal, perfect for a family dinner or a cozy lunch. Its rustic charm and deep flavors make it a beloved staple in Mexican homes.

instructions.title: Toast the Fideo Noodles
instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Add the fideo noodles and toast, stirring constantly, until they turn a deep golden brown. This step is crucial for flavor and texture. Be careful not to burn them.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tomato Sauce Base
instructions.text: While the noodles are toasting, combine the chopped Roma tomatoes, onion, and garlic cloves in a blender. Add 1/2 cup of chicken broth and blend until completely smooth. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl to remove any solids, ensuring a silky texture.

instructions.title: Sauté the Sauce
instructions.text: Once the fideo noodles are golden, carefully pour out any excess oil from the skillet. Pour the strained tomato sauce into the skillet with the toasted noodles. Add the remaining 1 1/2 cups of chicken broth, tomato paste, salt, and pepper. Stir well to combine.

instructions.title: Simmer the Fideo Seco
instructions.text: Bring the sauce to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and let it simmer. Cook for about 15-20 minutes, or until the noodles are tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Rest and Fluff
instructions.text: Once the fideo is cooked and the liquid is absorbed, remove the skillet from the heat. Keep it covered and let it rest for 5 minutes. This allows the noodles to fully absorb any remaining moisture and become perfectly tender. Fluff gently with a fork before serving.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Serve the Fideo Seco warm. Garnish generously with crumbled Cotija cheese, a drizzle of Mexican crema if desired, and freshly chopped cilantro. Enjoy this hearty and flavorful Mexican dish as a main course or a delicious side.

tips: Toasting the fideo noodles deeply golden brown is key. This step prevents them from becoming mushy and adds a nutty depth of flavor that is essential for Fideo Seco.
For a richer flavor, you can add a pinch of cumin or a small serrano pepper to the blender with the tomatoes and onion. Remove the pepper before serving for less heat.
Serve Fideo Seco with warm corn tortillas, a side of refried beans, or a simple green salad to complete your authentic Mexican meal.
